How I handle translations

I translate Spanish to English and English to Spanish. You get the price and the delivery date before I start.

My signed certification

Every translation comes with my signed statement that it’s complete and accurate and that I’m competent in both languages. I prepare it to meet USCIS and DMV requirements, but the agency decides whether to accept it.

The price up front

I charge by the page and give you the total before I start.

When you’ll have it

Usually 3 business days. If you’re in a hurry, I can have it in one business day for an extra charge.

In your language

I’ll walk you through it in Spanish or English, whichever works for you.

I only translate. I don’t give legal or immigration advice, and I can’t tell you which documents your case needs.

Good to know

Who translates
I’m a native speaker of both Spanish and English, with experience in translations submitted to USCIS and the Colorado DMV. Every translation includes my signed certification that I’m competent in both languages and that the translation is complete and accurate.
Turnaround
Usually 3 business days (Mon–Fri). There’s a one-day option if you’re in a hurry.
Notarizing something else
If you’d like me to come to you to notarize an affidavit or another document, the travel fee applies (see Pricing).
